learn: A dot adds half the note's value: a dotted half = 3 beats; a dotted quarter = 1 1/2 beats.
A dotted eighth = 3/4 of a beat, often paired with a sixteenth.
Dotted rhythms create a long-short "skipping" feel.
lessons.try: Clap dotted quarter + eighth patterns in "Auld Lang Syne".

learn: Count subdivisions: "1-and-2-and" for eighths; "1-e-and-a" for sixteenths.
A dotted quarter starting on beat 1 lasts through "2", and the eighth falls on "and".
Steady counting keeps rhythms accurate.
check: After a dotted quarter on beat 1, the eighth falls on...
lessons.try: Count and clap a measure: dotted quarter, eighth, half.

lessons.t: Dotted Rhythms in Marches and Anthems
learn: Marches often use dotted rhythms for a strong, bouncy feel.
"The Star-Spangled Banner" opens with a dotted rhythm.
Practising slowly helps master tricky dotted patterns.
check: Marches often use dotted rhythms for a...
Which song opens with a dotted rhythm?
lessons.try: Sing the opening of "The Star-Spangled Banner" and clap its rhythm.

learn: Syncopation shifts accents to weak beats or off-beats.
It creates surprise and energy.
A tied note across a beat often creates syncopation.
check: A tie across a beat often creates...
lessons.try: Clap a pattern with accents on the "and" of beats.

learn: Ragtime, jazz, Latin and funk music use lots of syncopation.
The clave rhythm is a key syncopated pattern in Afro-Cuban music.
Scott Joplin's "Maple Leaf Rag" (1899) is full of syncopation.
check: Which style uses lots of syncopation?
lessons.try: Learn the 3-2 son clave rhythm with two pencils.

learn: Use eighth-quarter-eighth patterns to place accents off the beat.
Ties connect notes across beats or bar lines.
Read and clap your patterns to check them.
lessons.try: Compose a four-measure syncopated rhythm.

learn: A major scale follows a pattern of whole (W) and half (H) steps: W W H W W W H.
C major uses all white keys. G major needs F♯ to fit the pattern.
Any note can start a major scale using this pattern.
check: W W H W W W H
W H W H W H W
H H H H H H H
lessons.try: Build a D major scale using the W-W-H-W-W-W-H pattern.

learn: The natural minor scale pattern is W H W W H W W.
A minor uses all white keys starting on A.
Every major key has a relative minor that shares its key signature: C major and A minor.
check: All white keys starting on A
The relative minor of C major is...
lessons.try: Play or sing the A minor scale.

lessons.t: Key Signatures and the Circle of Fifths
learn: The circle of fifths shows how keys relate. Moving clockwise adds a sharp; counter-clockwise adds a flat.
Order of sharps: F C G D A E B. Order of flats: B E A D G C F.
Key signatures save writing accidentals on every note.
check: Clockwise on the circle of fifths adds a...
lessons.try: Draw the circle of fifths with major keys.

units.t: The Bass Clef and Grand Staff

learn: The bass clef, or F clef, has two dots around the F line (fourth line from the bottom).
Bass lines from bottom: G, B, D, F, A ("Good Boys Do Fine Always").
Bass spaces: A, C, E, G ("All Cows Eat Grass").
check: The bass clef is also called the...
lessons.try: Name ten bass clef notes.

learn: The grand staff joins the treble and bass staves with a brace.
Middle C sits on a ledger line between them.
Piano music uses the grand staff: right hand on treble, left hand on bass.
check: Between the staves on a ledger line
lessons.try: Write middle C on both the treble and bass staff.

learn: Flute, violin and trumpet read treble clef.
Tuba, cello, bassoon and trombone read bass clef.
Viola reads alto clef, a C clef.
lessons.try: Find out which clef your favourite instrument uses.

learn: Intervals are named by counting letter names: C to E is a third (C-D-E).
Quality matters: major, minor, perfect, augmented, diminished.
C to E is a major third; C to E♭ is a minor third.
lessons.try: Name five intervals from C on a keyboard.

learn: A triad is a three-note chord built in thirds: root, third, fifth.
Major triads have a major third and perfect fifth: C-E-G.
Minor triads have a minor third: A-C-E.
lessons.try: Build major and minor triads on C, F and G.

learn: The I-IV-V-I progression is the backbone of much music.
The I-V-vi-IV progression appears in many pop songs.
Chord progressions create tension and release.
lessons.try: Play I-V-vi-IV in C major (C-G-Am-F) on an app or instrument.

learn: Strings sit in front; woodwinds behind them; brass behind woodwinds; percussion at the back.
First and second violins, violas, cellos and double basses make up the strings.
Seating helps balance the sound.
lessons.try: Draw a detailed orchestra seating chart.

learn: The conductor sets tempo, cues entrances, shapes dynamics and interprets the music.
The baton beats patterns; the left hand shows expression.
Conductors study the full score showing every instrument's part.
check: The conductor's left hand often shows...
lessons.try: Conduct a recording, beating the pattern and cueing instruments.

learn: Beethoven's Symphony No. 5 (1808) opens with a famous four-note motif.
Holst's "The Planets" (1916) depicts each planet's character.
Dvořák's "New World Symphony" (1893) was inspired by America.
check: The "New World Symphony" was inspired by...
lessons.try: Listen to the opening of Beethoven's Fifth and hum the motif.

learn: Medieval music (about 500-1400) included Gregorian chant, a single melody sung in Latin.
Renaissance music (1400-1600) added rich harmony with many voices (polyphony).
Hildegard of Bingen was a medieval composer and abbess.
lessons.try: Listen to a Gregorian chant and a Renaissance motet. Compare.

learn: Baroque (1600-1750): ornate music by Bach, Handel and Vivaldi; harpsichord common.
Classical (1750-1820): balanced, clear music by Haydn, Mozart and early Beethoven.
The piano replaced the harpsichord in the Classical era.
check: Which instrument was common in the Baroque?
lessons.try: Compare a harpsichord recording and a piano recording.

learn: Romantic (1820-1900): emotional, large-scale music by Chopin, Tchaikovsky and Brahms.
The 20th century brought new sounds: Debussy's Impressionism, Stravinsky's bold rhythms, and electronic music.
George Gershwin blended jazz and classical in "Rhapsody in Blue" (1924).
lessons.try: Listen to "Rhapsody in Blue" and describe how it mixes styles.

units.t: American Music: Blues, Jazz and Beyond

learn: The blues grew from African American work songs, spirituals and field hollers.
It uses the 12-bar form, blue notes (lowered pitches) and call-and-response.
W. C. Handy, called the "Father of the Blues", published "St. Louis Blues" in 1914.
check: Who was called the "Father of the Blues"?
lessons.try: Sing a simple 12-bar blues with your own lyrics.

learn: Jazz features improvisation, swing rhythm and syncopation.
Swing makes pairs of eighth notes long-short.
Ella Fitzgerald was famous for scat singing: improvising with nonsense syllables.
check: Who was famous for scat singing?
lessons.try: Try scat singing over a simple beat.

learn: Rock and roll grew in the 1950s from blues, gospel and country.
Hip-hop began in the Bronx, New York in the 1970s with DJs, MCs, breakdancing and graffiti.
American styles influenced music around the world.
check: Rock and roll grew in the...
Rock grew from blues, gospel and...
lessons.try: Make a timeline of American music styles from blues to hip-hop.

learn: African music often uses polyrhythms: several rhythms played at once.
The kora is a 21-string harp-lute from West Africa.
Mbira (thumb pianos) are played in Zimbabwe.
lessons.try: Clap a 3-against-2 polyrhythm with a partner.

learn: Chinese music uses the pentatonic scale and instruments like the erhu (two-string fiddle).
Japanese taiko drumming is powerful and athletic.
Indian classical music improvises on ragas over tala rhythm cycles.
lessons.try: Listen to the erhu and describe its sound.

lessons.t: Music of Latin America and Europe
learn: Brazilian samba uses lively percussion; Argentine tango is dramatic dance music.
Irish folk music uses the fiddle, tin whistle and bodhrán drum.
Spanish flamenco combines guitar, singing, clapping and dance.
lessons.try: Compare samba and tango recordings.

learn: Choose a key, meter and mood.
Write a motif: a short musical idea of a few notes.
Develop the motif through repetition, sequence (repeating at a different pitch) and variation.
check: Repeating a motif at a different pitch is a...
Before composing, choose a key, meter and...
lessons.try: Write a four-note motif and repeat it at different pitches.

learn: Melodies are built from phrases, often four measures long.
An antecedent phrase sounds like a question; the consequent sounds like an answer.
Ending on the tonic (do) sounds complete.
check: An antecedent phrase sounds like a...
Phrases are often how many measures?
lessons.try: Write a question phrase and an answer phrase.

learn: Write your melody on a staff with clef, key signature and time signature.
Free notation software can play your melody back.
Perform or record it and get feedback.
check: What goes at the start of the staff?
lessons.try: Notate your melody and perform it for your family.
